correctness.rationale: For finite k>=2 and every positive budget vector, the largest-modulus pivot provides a direct construction of any prescribed mixed-radix color with any one coordinate fixed. A surjection from colors to the r possible outcomes and the nonempty-intersection fallback yield exactly each selected neighborhood; the proof checks both set inclusions and exact action multiplicities. Conversely, the admissible one-neighborhood full-range frame has at most the product of other-agent actions many deterministic completions of each fixed action, proving all inequalities. Boundary k=2, b_i=1 and r=1 are covered. Executed bundled checker reports 15,920 slice assertions, 1,152 game representations and 21,760 budget tuples; experiments support but do not replace general proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 Ciardelli representation theorem proves existence but no multiplicity region. The two nearest published quantitative results, read in full, respectively establish r copies per neighbourhood and a sharp equal-copy root budget. Neither states or implies the sufficiency of all unequal vectors under complementary-product constraints; the mixed-modulus construction is an additional proof. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches for the claim, aliases, and mixed-grid hyperplanes identified no dominating result. Residual uncertainty about older mixed-level array and effectivity literature remains.
residual_risks: The mixed-alphabet array slice lemma or exact Pareto capacity condition may be established in unindexed hypergraph/polychromatic-array literature, even if not explicitly linked to game effectivity.
The full text of the older Goranko–Jamroga coalitional-effectivity work was not materially inspected, so quantitative implications beyond indexed text remain a risk.
No mathematical originality assertion can establish universal priority by searches alone.

value.rationale: The object is a natural action-resource tradeoff for the 2026 actual-effectivity representation theorem, not an arbitrary sliced numerical exercise. The claim classifies the full universal Pareto feasible region of heterogeneous per-agent action-copy budgets, strictly generalizing the published sharp symmetric root bound: for three agents and twelve outcomes (3,4,4) is feasible while its equal-budget rule uses (4,4,4). It supplies a mixed-level constructive realization for every feasible vector plus a matching worst-case impossibility witness. It does not claim per-frame minima or novelty of the abstract array technique.
